title: BRIDGE: Behavior-Guided Residual Integration with Dual-Frequency Graph Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2605.22073v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Multimodal recommendation improves item representations by combining visual, textual, and collaborative signals, but stronger cross-view alignment does not always improve ranking. Our diagnostics on Amazon Baby show that direct consistency has an effective range: moderate alignment helps, while stronger alignment suppresses recommendation-specific variation. We also observe a clear spectral split: low-frequency components capture shared structure, whereas higher-frequency components retain more private ranking signal. Based on these findings, we propose BRIDGE, a behavior-guided residual integration framework built on dual-frequency graph evidence. translated_title: BRIDGE：行为引导的残差整合与双频图证据
translated_abstract: 多模态推荐通过结合视觉、文本和协同信号来改善物品表示，但更强的跨视图对齐并不总能提升排序性能。我们在Amazon Baby数据集上的诊断显示，直接一致性存在有效范围：适度的对齐有助于性能提升，而更强的对齐则会抑制推荐特有的变异性。我们还观察到明显的频谱分离：低频成分捕获共享结构，而高频成分保留更多私有排序信号。基于这些发现，我们提出了BRIDGE，一个建立在双频图证据上的行为引导残差整合框架。BRIDGE将模型分为三个部分：DFGE将图平滑的ID、视觉和文本通道分解为频谱带；BEN将仅训练时的共用户重叠转化为有符号的候选证据；CRI仅在训练过程中将该证据应用于基础Top-K候选集内部。
tldr: BRIDGE提出了一种行为引导的残差整合框架，通过双频图证据分离和候选集内证据应用，解决了多模态推荐中对齐强度与排序性能之间的非线性关系。
en_tdlr: BRIDGE proposes a behavior-guided residual integration framework with dual-frequency graph evidence, addressing the nonlinear relationship between alignment strength and ranking performance in multimodal recommendation.
